historical_references.reference: Sidhant Kaumudi, also known as Sidhanta Shiromani, was a renowned Indian mathematician, astronomer, and philosopher from the 11th century. He is considered one of the last great mathematicians of the Classical Indian mathematical tradition and is best known for his work in trigonometry, algebra, and astronomical calculations. His most famous works include the Sidhanta Siromani and the Karana-Grantha, which were comprehensive works on mathematics and astronomy.

Another famous Sidhant is Siddhanta Ashwatamana, who lived during the 3rd century BCE. He is best known for his Siddhantas, a collection of astronomical texts that were widely used in ancient India. These texts contained tables of astronomical data, rules for calculating planetary positions, and instructions for constructing astronomical instruments. The Siddhantas played a crucial role in the development of Indian astronomy and influenced later works such as the Surya Siddhanta and the Aryabhata.
